5: - Preserve the existing typed public API: `prefix(items: list[int]) -> list[int]`.
6: - Accumulate a running total and append it after each input value, producing inclusive prefix sums with the same length as the input.
7: - Return a fresh list without changing the input. Empty input naturally returns `[]`; negative values and zeros use ordinary integer addition.
8: - The implementation uses only the Python standard library and takes O(n) time and O(n) space for the returned list.
9: - Six unittest methods cover positive, empty, negative, mixed/zero, single-item, and input-preservation behavior.
10: - Add `prefix_many(cases: list[tuple]) -> list`, calling `prefix(*case)` once per tuple in input order. Empty input returns `[]`; the first exception propagates unchanged and stops further calls.
